q: What are the emissions from recycling lithium ion batteries?
title: Lithium ion battery recycling emissions
short: It depends on the route. Shredding to black mass uses mainly electricity; furnace routes add fuel and burn the graphite and electrolyte; chemical leaching routes use acids and reagents. Report per tonne of batteries processed, and state which route you use.

ul: Electricity and fuel by process step.
Output: black mass or recovered metals.

p: Recovered metals can lower a buyer's footprint compared with mined metal, but only with records of the recovery route and quantities.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
